_comment: Plain-English purpose line per skill, shown on the hub skills reference. Curated by hand; skills missing here fall back to the first sentence of their SKILL.md description. Keep each line one sentence, no jargon, no em-dashes.
agent-docs-hub: Publishes and updates every agent's user guide and release notes on this hub, screenshots included.
agentic-harness-designer: Designs and reviews AI agent systems as a whole: the tools, permissions, safety rails and workflows around the model, not just the model choice.
assumption-checker: Reads a plan or strategy document and lists the hidden assumptions, missing evidence and contradictions before you act on it.
audience-content-system: Writes content calibrated to one specific publication and audience level, for example a beginner-focused newsletter.
automation-discovery: Digs through real work history (AI sessions, Slack, tickets) to find and prove which recurring jobs are worth automating, then builds the chosen one.
brain-dump-processor: Turns a messy voice memo or rambling note into cleanly separated ideas, evaluates which are worth pursuing, and files them.
branded-image-prompting: A prompting guide that keeps every generated image on brand: colors, typography, composition and recurring formats.
broll-pipeline: Turns a finished talking-head video into one with animated motion graphics inserted at exactly the right moments.
browser-qa: Tests web pages like a professional: performance, errors, responsive and accessibility checks, click-through flows, with screenshots as evidence.
buzz-comms: Posts to and reads from Buzz, the private team chat where humans and agents coordinate.
case-data-normalization: Turns messy case facts into one clean ledger of dates, parties, amounts, categories and review status.
chief-of-staff: Runs the daily operating rhythm: morning briefing, coordination across tasks and follow-ups, end-of-day review.
citation-guard: Checks that every claim in a draft actually matches the evidence it cites: the source must exist and say what is claimed.
clean-my-ai-harness: Maps everything the agent is configured with and proposes a safe cleanup of stale instructions, memories and skills.
content-radar: Watches followed influencers daily and delivers a rated morning digest to Telegram, with one-tap booking of reading slots.
cron-audit: The weekly report of every scheduled job: what runs, what has gone silent, what is switched off.
current-info-search: Sends web research through a search API built for fresh information instead of the harness's built-in search.
deep-research: Deep, multi-source, fact-checked research: the question is broken down, primary sources read, and every claim adversarially verified.
deterministic-retrieval-map: Lookup tables that say exactly which document sections matter for each case type, so retrieval stops guessing.
document-chunking-tagging: Splits ingested documents into addressable, tagged sections so agents can cite the exact place a fact came from.
end-feature: The ship-time closeout of a feature: tests verified on the real build, screenshots taken, docs published to the hub, announcement material generated, Ship Card written.
essay-illustration-gallery: Illustrates a finished essay end to end: picks the image-worthy moments, generates consistent images, and builds the gallery page.
feature-blueprint: The pre-development gate: press release, user tests, release-note draft, guide updates and marketing pack, all before one line of code.
frontend-taste: Stronger design instincts for anything web-built: varied layouts, real typography, restrained color, and screenshot-verified results.
goal-prompt-generator: Turns a fuzzy plan into a bounded objective for an agent, with a definition of done, hard limits and stop conditions.
heavy-file-ingestion: Converts big, agent-hostile files (large PDFs, decks, spreadsheets) into light readable artifacts before any analysis begins.
html-artifacts: Turns dense output (plans, research, reviews, comparisons) into one polished, self-contained HTML page.
human-gate: The stop line for high-stakes work: agents prepare, draft and validate; a human reviews, signs, sends, files or pays.
image-gateway: Generates or edits images through one API with a single command and no per-call setup.
image-model-arena: Builds side-by-side comparison pages for image-generation models running the same prompts.
kara-release-notes: Kara's ship ritual: write the notes entry, release to the self-update feed, publish the updates pages.
link-digest: Summarizes and rates any link Thomas shares in Telegram, and books an evening reading slot when it is worth the time.
media-transcription: Transcribes audio and video files into clean transcripts with timestamps, chapters and speaker labels.
meeting-synthesis: Turns a meeting recording or transcript into takeaways, decisions with owners, action items and open questions.
meetingbrief: Prepares a meeting: pulls the calendar event, researches the external attendees, and delivers the brief to Telegram.
my-voice: Encodes how Thomas actually writes, per context, so drafts sound like him instead of like an AI.
nle-assistant: Drives the video editor (DaVinci Resolve) directly: silence removal, subclips and timelines built inside the real project.
open-agent-engine: The runner playbook for the Linear task queue: claim exactly one task, do the scoped work, leave receipts.
open-brain-case-store: Keeps the normalized case-file records inside Open Brain instead of a local database.
openbrain: Search, capture and log to Open Brain, the durable knowledge base of decisions, meetings, people and context.
packet-export: Packages reviewed outputs into an editable folder and PDF: draft, citation map, checklist and source manifest.
page-testing-memory: Keeps page-specific testing facts (selectors, test accounts, cleanup quirks) in repo-local runbooks where they belong.
para-ai-filing-context: Teaches agents the PARA filing logic before they save, export or publish any deliverable, so nothing gets misfiled.
para-filing-auditor: Audits and reorganizes the PARA filing systems on Dropbox and Google Drive, always plan-first with explicit approval.
para-organizer: Sets up or cleans a PARA folder structure (Projects, Areas, Resources, Archives) on the local file system.
pdf-document-ingestion: Converts PDFs, scans and forms into markdown or tables with stable references back to the exact source spot.
project-intake-router: Sets up a new project properly before work starts: PARA home, folder structure, brief, milestones, skills and human gates.
radio-edit: Locks the spoken narrative of a video first, as a transcript-driven rough cut, before any visuals are touched.
reading-pack-builder: Builds a controlled local reading page from a pile of documents so review happens in one place.
release-briefing: Turns gathered data about a significant release in the field into a clear, decision-ready briefing.
ringer: The verified-swarm playbook: batches of work routed to cheap workers, with executable checks deciding pass or fail.
self-pr-merge: Reviews and merges Thomas's own pull requests with real discipline despite GitHub's self-approval limits.
session-operating-map: A per-project map of parallel agent sessions so lanes of work stay named and never collide.
session-to-skill-extractor: Reviews a finished work session for reusable patterns and drafts them as new or updated skills.
site-publisher: Publishes a finished page to the personal or company website as a real, share-ready URL.
skill-promoter: The weekly sweep that finds skills created locally on any agent surface and promotes new ones into the shared GitHub catalog, so every skill reaches all agents and this reference page.
skills-status: Shows every catalog skill with a check of whether it is installed in the agent you are talking to.
sqlite-case-store: A local SQLite database for source documents, chunks, normalized records and validation results.
stakeholder-update-email: After work ships, sends or drafts a short, truthful update email to the person who needs to know.
start-here: The front-door reflex for every task: recap open loops, run the routing test out loud, pick the lightest tool that still leaves an inspectable result.
testing-runbook-creator: Ensures testing discoveries get written into runbooks instead of dying in the chat where they were found.
visible-delegation: Lets one agent drive another in a shared terminal session so delegated work stays visible.
weekly-signal-diff: Reviews a defined set of inputs on a cadence and reports only what changed since last time.
